title: Learning bagpipes and marching in the St. Patrick's parade
summary: He adopted a Scottish identity in New York, learned pipes from Mr. Gallagher and marched for years.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Last Friday was St. Patrick's Day and I just happened to notice last Saturday. I just happened to notice, looking in the Musicians Union book in New York City, the only bagpipe player we have registered in the music book is James Maxwell. How'd you go about that, Jim?
Yeah. Well, you know, I told you my background. I don't think I can really claim to be pure

Scotch or Irish by any means but I've always loved the bagpipes. When I first came to New York, people asked me what I was, I'd say American. And that's not a good answer in New York, you know. In New York you've got to be an ethnic. So they'd say, "You've got a Scottish name, you must be Scottish. So I decided I'd be Scottish. Some of my ancestors did come from Scotland and I did hear a lot about it around the house, I heard some Scottish words, you know. I guess if there were any two outstanding cultures it would be Scotch and Irish.

But I would go to hear these pipe bands when they'd come to the Garden and tears would pour out of my eyes. So my wife bought me some pipes about 30 years ago and I went to a teacher and learned to play them. And it was kind of funny, in the beginning he gave me free lessons, he wouldn't take any money. And it came around January and he said, well, it's time to be measured up for the kilt. I said, I don't want a kilt, I just want to play the bagpipes. He said, well, you don't have to march in the parade but you can't do it without a kilt. I said I didn't plan on marching in the parade and he said, well, "Just because I gave you free lessons doesn't mean you're obliged to do it." I said, "Okay, Mr. Gallagher, okay." So I marched in the parade on St. Patrick's Day, walked right down by NBC and thought, Oh, God, I hope nobody comes out and sees me.
So for five or six years I marched in every St. Patrick's Day, I'd march in the parade.
Did you do it last Saturday?

No, last Saturday I was down in Florida. I haven't done it -- the band I was in sort of broke up about 10 years ago. And actually, I think the Sanitation Department took it over. They have a pipe band now and they wear the same kilt that we wore. And Mr. Gallagher retired to Las Vegas or some place.

He wound up traveling with the Kim Sisters, do you remember them? Three Korean girls that played all the instruments. And they decided they wanted to learn bagpipe, and they must have given him a fortune because he packed it in and went off with the Kim Sisters.
And he was an artist. God, he was a great piper.
